Why was it hyped up?

Context in the Past

The anime has a plethora of Western influences, from film noir to old western cowboy movies. Western music has a significant impact as well, in both actual soundtrack music that is also widely praised, as well as references to popular songs in episode titles ("Honky Tonk Woman" and "Sympathy for the Devil"). Because of these influences, it is widely considered a good 'gateway' anime for people in the West, as many elements are more familiar to them. The English dub is widely praised as one of the best in history, some even consider it better than the original Japanese due to the wider array of accents and its western influence as a whole.

Modern Context

The context for the past still holds up today, as well as the tendency for people to often cite opinions that the animation quality was ahead of its time and still holds up today. Despite not having more releases in the franchise beyond a movie and some manga, Bebop has gotten a recent Bluray rerelease that has sold well in both Japan and America.

Some peoples think that Bebop was more popular in the west than in Japan. This is due to lack of Japanese references mixed with Japan's xenophobic tendencies, as well as it's popularity in the west leading to many reruns on anime programming such as Toonami that kept it relevant.
